payload.title: Wedding Planning Checklist Month by Month, From 12 Months Out
payload.refresh_mode: in place, URL kept, no slug change, no redirect
payload.excerpt: A 12 month wedding checklist, month by month: what to book first, when to send invitations, a destination wedding track and a printable recap table.
key_takeaways: At 12 months out, settle what you will spend, the guest count, the style and the venue, then book key suppliers and send save-the-dates at 10 to 11 months.
At 6 to 7 months out, choose rings and stationery and apply for any new passport, then send invitations with travel details at 4 to 5 months.
Use the final month for the legal and supplier check, and the last 2 weeks to hand every job you can to someone else.

If marrying in Australia, your Notice of Intended Marriage must reach your celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding, and on an Australian passport you should allow at least 6 weeks for a new or renewed one.

faq.q: Can you plan a wedding in 11 months?
faq.a: Yes. Start with the 10 to 11 months out block and fold the 12 month tasks into your first few weeks: what you will spend, the guest count, the style and the venue. For a destination wedding, check passports and the embassy's document requirements in the same first weeks, since those steps have lead times you cannot compress.

faq.q: Is 2 months enough time to plan a wedding?
faq.a: For a small wedding in Australia, it can be, provided your NOIM reaches your celebrant at least 1 month before the wedding. Overseas is harder: a new or renewed passport needs at least 6 weeks from lodging, and legalising documents can take longer in peak holiday periods.

faq.q: What do I need for a wedding checklist?
faq.a: A list of tasks grouped by when they need doing, with an owner beside each one. Cover spend, guests, venue, suppliers, attire, stationery, rings, legal paperwork, travel and final confirmations. For a destination wedding, add passports, documents for the overseas authority, room blocks and insurance.

faq.q: When should you lodge the Notice of Intended Marriage?
faq.a: As at November 2026, give the NOIM to your authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding. Lodging early, as soon as the date and celebrant are booked, removes the deadline from the final month. The form can be witnessed in person or via audio-visual link.

faq.q: What do couples forget before their wedding?
faq.a: The small, practical things: meals for suppliers, a wet-weather plan, someone to collect gifts and cards, transport home at the end of the night and an emergency kit. Overseas, add original documents in hand luggage and bookings that match the name on each passport.
